G'day all,

Long time rustacean here but new to RFL and the LKML.

I have put together an MVP of Rust WMI abstractions as a requirement to implement a keyboard backlight driver for my laptop (Clevo NL57AU) in Rust.

Could use some feedback on this if you have some time, specifically;

  • Acceptable level of documentation for an initial submission - noticed a lot of the existing device abstractions have examples etc.
  • Testing requirements and ideas for what I might be able to unit-test
  • LKML submission sequencing - the driver has a couple of dependencies including Markus's led abstractions and a review from a vendor (Tuxedo) - should I hold off submitting the WMI abstractions until these are complete?

https://github.com/nick42d/linux/pull/2

The prototypical device driver is implemented in the stacked PR for your reference as well.

Cheers Nick

should I hold off submitting the WMI abstractions until these are complete?

No, you can submit it whenever you feel it is ready enough, but you will want to mention clearly the dependency; otherwise, it can be confusing.

Regarding documentation and testing: that is part of getting submissions ready for upstream. How much polish it needs depends a bit on the maintainer/subsystem, but docs and testing are the sort of thing that if it is not done initially, then it may never get done :) It also helps reviewers, so it is good to add it before submitting. I would suggest taking a look at what we have elsewhere, to give you an idea of what you could do.

I hope that helps, and welcome!

Cheers Miguel - much appreciated! I'll look to align my documentation / testing approach with some of the other bus driver abstractions like PCI, USB. Hopefully I can have this out to the mailing list within the next week.
